svg.title: MCP mid-interaction authorization: 401 insufficient_authorization + RAR remediation + one-shot token (pre-authorization elicitation, pending operation, session token preserved)

g.text: MCP mid-interaction authorization: 401 insufficient_authorization + RAR remediation + one-shot token
(pre-authorization elicitation, pending operation, session token preserved)
1. Transfer: the tool discovers it needs a per-operation grant
The SDK's isError result is discarded and rewritten.
Rule: 4xx ⇒ nothing executed for this request.
4. Client remediation: ONE-SHOT token (request id=7 HELD, LLM unaware)
op_X stays awaiting_authorization until TTL → failed.
T2 is NOT stored. T1 remains the session token.
5. Replay with T2, resume from checkpoint, burn T2
6. Later calls keep using the SESSION token
8. A one-shot token cannot be reused
phases 4-5 again: a fresh one-shot token for op_Y
9. Guard: challenge after a side effect (non-atomic tool)
With known payees nothing is committed first: one 401 carries N authorization_details,
so one consent and one one-shot token cover the whole batch.
• Tools never advertise the requirement; it is discovered during execution.
• Operation token: authorization_details only, NO scope, short TTL, no refresh, burned by jti at commit.
• Session token (mcp:basic) is never replaced; it keeps serving every other request.
• Elicitation is UX (intent + "something is in course"), never the authorization itself.
• Atomic challenge: allowed only while nothing has been committed in the request.
• (Mcp-Session-Id, JSON-RPC id) identifies the pending operation across the replay.
• Requires JSON response mode; the client raises the request timeout (5 min) for held requests.
